newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed higher as the overall market continued to take a breather from its downtrend since mid-March, traders and analysts said.

June Standard & Poor's 500s have steadily inched higher since Monday when they fell to 736.70, and came close to testing the April 9 high of 774.60, which corresponds to major trendline resistance at 774.00 to 774.50.
"The near-term downtrend was too steep -- you needed a lift," said Jay Hohmann, head trader of stock index trading at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
Traders said expiration-related buying contributed to the market's firm tone. April options on S&P futures expired at the close.
Several traders noted light arbitrage buy and sell programs throughout the day, but they said volume was too light to generate much momentum. They estimated volume at 62,000 contracts.
"At times there were just pockets of air and you couldn't trade anything," one floor trader said.
Arbitrage buy programs were at a premium of about 5.00 points to cash.
Arbitrage sell programs were at a premium of 3.10 points.
Fair value for June S&Ps was at 4.75 points to cash.
A sharp rise in Microsoft Corp stock, coupled with the recovery in the U.S. T-bond market, also supported S&Ps, traders said.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were up 4.15 at 770.25, NYSE Composites were up 1.85 at 404.70, KCBT Value Lines were 1.00 higher at 690.50, Nikkeis were 345 higher at 18,430, Midcap 400s were down 0.25 at 253.25 and Nasdaq 100s were up 7.25 at 822.25. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
